verdicts.reason: CEILING HALF HELD, FLOOR HALF REFUTED - and the floor half is the finding's own headline. Every sub-cite is verbatim true: skilldata.xml:4-6 is <id>1000</id><displayname>6000</displayname>, strings.json["6000"]='Light Stance Mastery', :7 is <passive>1</passive>, ten <level> blocks value 1..10; StatsManager.as:740-742 is exactly IntStat(1000,1)/(1001,1)/(1002,1); §1t99s0§.as:3262 is _loc1_*(0.5+0.4*§1t4421s0§*0.1) and :3265 is _loc1_*(1+0.2*§1t4422s0§*0.1). m=10 gives exactly 0.90 and 1.20; m=9 gives 0.86 and 1.18. So the ceiling is 10 and the ledger's 'MASTERY-9' label is dead. But the inference 'so mastery is 1-indexed with floor 1' does not follow and is false. The seed at :740-742 sits inside initNewPlayer (StatsManager.as:689) - it is a fresh-save default, not an index base. NPCs take their mastery from XMLNpc.getMastery, which ends 'return 0;' at :685 when the npc has no such <skill> row, and my census of npcdata.xml finds only 76 of 495 npcs carry skill 1000 (77 carry 1001, 79 carry 1002) - so 419 npcs run the very curve this finding is about at mastery 0. CONTRADICTION LENS: 'floor 1' collides head-on with five already-upheld findings that evaluate this same curve at mastery 0 - [[combat-core/reach-table-is-mastery-zero-not-a-ceiling]], [[combat-core/stance-reach-is-mastery-zero-base]], [[combat-core/300-200-100-is-base-not-ceiling]], [[skills-meters/reach-triple-is-a-floor-not-a-ceiling]] and [[skills-meters/stance-damage-ceiling-is-mastery-10]] ('M in 0..10'). Refuting costs nothing on the ceiling: mastery-10 is banked five separate ways already, including [[skills-meters/stance-damage-ceiling-is-mastery-10]] at 6 critics and strings.json["8131"]='Light Stance Mastery Level 10.' The ledger sentence therefore does fall - on those siblings, not on this one. Corrected domain filed as NF-S27B-1.

new_findings.text: CONTRADICTION SETTLED: the stance-mastery domain is [0,10], not [1,10]. The 1 in StatsManager.as:740-742 (IntStat(1000,1)/(1001,1)/(1002,1)) is a NEW-PLAYER DEFAULT, not an index base - the enclosing function is initNewPlayer at StatsManager.as:689. For NPCs the value comes from XMLNpc.getMastery, which ends 'return 0;' at :685 when the npc carries no matching <skill> row, and a census of reference/extracted/npcdata.xml shows only 76 of 495 <npc> rows carry skill 1000 (77 carry 1001, 79 carry 1002; of those that do, 74 each are at <lvl>10</lvl> and the rest at 2-3). So 419 of 495 npcs evaluate the stance curve at mastery 0. EnemyElite.as:89 declares 'var balancedMastery:int = 0;' before its getMastery reads at :103-105, and the web fighter class declares all three fields '= 0' at §1t99s0§.as:107/:109/:111. This is NOT a build-parity split: web v0.717 and android v0.682 agree the field is a plain int defaulting to 0. Consequence for the rewrite: a config that clamps mastery to >= 1 mis-prices every generic mob's stance damage AND reach - Light damage would floor at 0.54 instead of 0.50 and Heavy reach at 0.54x instead of 0.50x of base. The mastery-10 CEILING is unaffected and stands.

new_findings.text: CONTRADICTION SETTLED between two findings that both already survive: LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:1630 banks 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE is NOT a lock notice, it is the reload/crit meter's own low-end label' while :160 banks it is 'a literally true refusal'. Both are true, because they are the same constant written in two files. The caption's display rule is §1t113s0§.as:328 ratio = (reload-48)/(maxreload-48), negatives clamped to 0 at :329-332, shown at :336 iff ratio == 0, i.e. iff reload <= 48. The switch gate is §1t99s0§.as:3048-3050 '§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48', reinforced by the early return at :3058-3061 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48) return;'. The two predicates are complements except on ONE value: at reload == 48 exactly, the bar renders 0% and the caption is on screen while the switch is legal. That single-value overlap is a shipped cosmetic off-by-one, not a disagreement between the findings. Neither reading should be dropped in the rewrite; write the caption as a meter-state readout whose threshold is the gate.
new_findings.lane_impact: L8 ui-hud + L5 combat-core: one number, 48, drives both the bar's zero point and the stance gate. Ship them from a single config constant so the caption cannot drift out of sync with the refusal - and reproduce the reload==48 boundary rather than 'fixing' it.

new_findings.text: BUILD PARITY, LABELLED: the three-state caption on the Focus/crit bar exists only in web v0.717. Android v0.682's BattleUI.updateReload (BattleUI.as:259-263) is two lines - 'this.reloadbar.bar.scaleX = percentage;' and 'this.crittext.visible = percentage >= 1 && this.reloadbar.visible;'. There is no ratio==0 branch, no grey label, and no Snd_criticalDamage call; string 960 has no row in the android table at all. The web twin §1t5205s0§ (§1t113s0§.as:326-361) instead takes the RAW (reload, maxreload) pair, normalises it in the UI at :328 with a 48 dead zone, and drives three states plus the crit sound. Android normalises player-side with a 24 dead zone before the call - MCSPlayer.as:3272 'StageManager.getBattleUI().updateReload((this.reload - 24) / (this.maxreload - 24));'. So the widget is architecturally different, not just differently tuned: any port that reads the android reload bar as the same component will ship a two-state meter with the wrong dead zone and no stance caption.
new_findings.lane_impact: L8 ui-hud: build the Focus bar from the WEB shape - UI-side normalisation, dead zone 48, three states (grey 960 / hidden / black 175 + Snd_criticalDamage). The android two-state version is the wrong build's widget.
